Unified Healthcare Appointment and Immunization Tracking System is a web-based comprehensive healthcare management platform designed to eliminate record fragmentation across hospitals, streamline appointment scheduling, manage maternal and child immunization schedules, and optimize clinical doctor workloads. Patient medical information often remains isolated within individual hospital databases, leading to delayed emergency treatment, redundant diagnostic tests, and untracked vaccination milestones. The system consolidates medical histories into a unified record accessible to authorized healthcare providers across participating institutions.

The system supports Patient, Doctor, Hospital Staff, and Hospital Administrator workflows. Built on the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, Node.js) and integrated with a Python Flask Machine Learning microservice, it manages patient registration, digital ABHA ID authentication, online appointment booking, unified medical history tracking, inter-hospital emergency referrals, government maternal ID (RCH/PICME) tracking, and multi-language accessibility across six regional languages (English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam). Machine learning algorithms, specifically Gradient Boosting Classifiers, are implemented to predict appointment urgency types (Emergency, Consultation, Follow-up, Vaccination, General Checkup) and calculate doctor workload risk scores (0-100) for effective clinical schedule balancing.

The application utilizes React.js with TailwindCSS for a responsive client interface, Node.js and Express.js for core REST API services, MongoDB with Mongoose for document storage, node-cron for automated background reminder scheduling, and Python Flask for machine learning inference. Digital health identity is integrated using standard ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) Sandbox API specifications. Inter-hospital referral features allow instant transfer of emergency medical summaries, current medications, allergies, and diagnoses during patient transfers. An automated background reminder scheduler runs continuously to notify patients of upcoming appointments, follow-ups, medication schedules, and child vaccination due dates.

The main objective of the system is to provide an integrated, intelligent environment for healthcare administration and clinical record continuity. By combining electronic health records, predictive machine learning models, ABHA digital health identities, maternal-child health tracking, automated reminder schedulers, and robust API services, the platform establishes a reliable foundation for modern healthcare management.

Healthcare delivery systems depend heavily on continuous patient information access, timely clinical decision-making, and proactive preventive care. Patients frequently consult multiple healthcare providers across different hospitals. When medical histories are maintained in isolated hospital databases, doctors lack access to previous diagnoses, prescriptions, lab results, and known allergies.

The Unified Healthcare Appointment and Immunization Tracking System is a web-based comprehensive healthcare platform proposed to address these challenges. It provides a centralized environment for managing patient appointments, consolidating electronic health records across hospitals, authenticating national ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) health IDs, tracking maternal and child immunization schedules using government-issued registration IDs (RCH/PICME), delivering multi-language UI accessibility, and balancing clinical doctor workloads using machine learning.

The system incorporates clinical patient datasets to train predictive models. Machine learning algorithms, including Gradient Boosting Classifiers and Random Forest models, are trained to perform two main tasks: predicting appointment urgency types (Emergency, Consultation, Follow-up, Vaccination, General Checkup) based on patient clinical parameters, and computing clinical workload risk scores (0-100) to assist in balancing doctor consultation schedules.

The platform supports four principal user roles: Patient, Doctor, Hospital Staff, and Hospital Administrator. Patients can search for doctors, book appointment slots, view their unified medical history, track vaccination due dates, link ABHA health IDs, select their preferred language, and receive automated reminders. Doctors can manage consultation slots, view complete patient histories, record diagnoses and prescriptions, initiate inter-hospital emergency referrals, and review their workload risk scores. Hospital Staff assist in patient onboarding, slot management, and vaccination logging. Hospital Administrators oversee doctor onboarding, department configuration, and overall system operations.

The application integrates React.js for the responsive frontend user interface, Node.js and Express.js for backend RESTful APIs, node-cron for automated background reminder scheduling, MongoDB for flexible document database storage, Python Flask for machine learning inference, and scikit-learn for model training. The system is designed as a production-ready web application providing a scalable solution for modern healthcare delivery.

The primary objective of this project is to construct a unified digital healthcare platform that eliminates data fragmentation across medical facilities. By maintaining a single portable Electronic Health Record (EHR) accessible across authorized institutions, the system aims to improve clinical decision-making speed during emergency referrals, prevent duplicate diagnostic testing, and ensure uninterrupted long-term patient care continuity.

Additionally, the platform integrates automated preventive care management for maternal and pediatric health. By linking government-issued registration references (such as RCH / ABHA IDs) with automated dose calculators and notification schedulers, the system ensures timely antenatal checkups and child immunization tracking regardless of where care is delivered. Multi-language UI localization (across 6 regional languages) and machine-learning triage models further optimize patient accessibility and clinical doctor workload balancing.

The scope of this project encompasses a full-stack MERN (MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, Node.js) web application serving four distinct user roles: Patients, Doctors, Hospital Staff, and Hospital Administrators. The core functionality centers on a consolidated electronic health record (EHR) module that tracks patient diagnoses, active prescriptions, laboratory results, and documented allergies across participating facilities. Additionally, the scope includes an inter-hospital referral data transfer module that allows emergency medical summaries to be shared instantly between hospitals during critical care patient transfers, alongside digital health identity verification using national ABHA Sandbox API standards.

To support preventive healthcare delivery, the system includes dedicated maternal health tracking linked with government-issued RCH / PICME registration IDs, as well as a child immunization tracking module featuring automated dose milestone scheduling and background node-cron email reminders. Accessibility is enhanced through multi-language UI localization across six regional languages (English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam). Furthermore, the scope integrates a Python Flask Machine Learning microservice executing trained Gradient Boosting Classifiers to predict appointment urgency triage types and compute clinical doctor workload risk scores (0–100) for schedule optimization. All data transactions are secured using JSON Web Tokens (JWT), bcryptjs password hashing, and role-based access control.

In traditional healthcare delivery, patient records are maintained independently by each hospital or clinic in isolated electronic systems or paper files. When a patient visits a new hospital or is transferred during a medical emergency, doctors cannot access previous diagnoses, active prescriptions, lab results, or known allergies. National digital health identification such as ABHA ID is often absent, preventing record interoperability.

Maternal care and child immunization tracking are often handled through physical paper cards or isolated regional registers. Mothers frequently miss antenatal checkups or vaccination due dates due to lack of automated background reminders. Language barriers in rural areas further hinder patient interaction. Furthermore, appointment scheduling relies on manual queuing, and doctor consultation workloads are assigned without considering patient clinical severity.

The existing approach represents a fragmented healthcare environment in which medical history continuity, emergency referral data sharing, digital health identity, immunization tracking, and doctor workload management operate in silos without an integrated technological framework.
Fragmented health records – medical histories are isolated within individual hospital databases.
Lack of digital health identity – absence of ABHA ID integration prevents seamless cross-hospital patient identification.
Delayed emergency care – emergency physicians lack immediate access to transferred patients' medical histories and allergies during referrals.
Untracked immunizations and missed checkups – physical paper cards and lack of automated cron reminders lead to missed vaccination doses.
Redundant diagnostic testing – doctors order duplicate lab tests due to missing historical medical records.
Language accessibility barriers – interfaces lack regional language support for rural patients.
Manual appointment triage – appointments are scheduled without evaluating clinical urgency or patient risk.
Unbalanced doctor workloads – consultation schedules do not account for cumulative patient severity.

The proposed Unified Healthcare Appointment and Immunization Tracking System establishes a web-based platform that unifies patient health records, integrates national ABHA digital health identities, streamlines online appointment booking, automates maternal and child immunization tracking, dispatches automated background reminders via node-cron, supports six regional languages, and applies machine learning for clinical triage and doctor workload balancing. The system integrates a MERN stack web application with a Python Flask machine learning microservice.

The proposed architecture separates application responsibilities into a presentation layer (React.js + TailwindCSS + i18n), backend REST API layer (Node.js & Express.js + node-cron + ABHA API), database layer (MongoDB), and machine learning service layer (Flask & scikit-learn). MongoDB stores document collections for users, doctors, appointments, slots, maternal records, immunizations, and medical history, while the ML service exposes endpoints for appointment type prediction and workload risk scoring.

Clinical doctor workload risk score calculation and schedule optimization

The Unified Healthcare Appointment and Immunization Tracking System follows a multi-tier microservice architecture. The React.js frontend application with i18n localization acts as the presentation layer. The Express.js backend handles business logic, session management, node-cron background reminder execution, ABHA Sandbox API integration, and CRUD operations. The Python Flask service acts as an independent machine learning microservice for model inference. MongoDB serves as the data persistence layer for all application records.
The architecture can be described through the following layers:

Presentation Layer – React.js single-page application styled with TailwindCSS following Organic Modernist design principles, featuring i18n multi-language support (English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam).

Application / API Layer – Node.js and Express.js RESTful web services managing routing, authentication middleware, ABHA API integration, node-cron background reminder scheduler, and database operations.
Machine Learning Microservice Layer – Python Flask service executing pre-trained Gradient Boosting Classifier models for triage and workload risk scoring.
Data Layer – MongoDB database maintaining document collections for users, doctors, appointments, slots, maternal records, immunizations, and unified medical history.
Integration & Security Layer – ABHA Sandbox API integration, JWT authentication, bcryptjs password hashing, and CORS middleware for safe cross-origin communication.
Visualization Layer – Interactive clinical dashboards, doctor workload risk indicators, multi-language controls, and vaccination schedule timelines.
Architecture Flow: Streamlit Interface → FastAPI Services → Pydantic Validation → SQLite / ML / Optimization Processing → Prediction, Index & Allocation → Streamlit Visualization

Step 2 – Appointment Booking: Patient selects doctor, slot, and inputs clinical details.
Step 3 – ML Triage Execution: Flask service predicts appointment type and patient risk score.
Step 4 – Workload Score Calculation: Doctor schedule risk score is updated.
Step 5 – Clinical Consultation: Doctor accesses unified history and records diagnosis/prescription.
Step 6 – Maternal / Child Care Linking: Records are registered under RCH ID and vaccination dates scheduled.

MongoDB is used as the document-oriented database for the system. It provides high flexibility for storing complex, nested medical records, prescriptions, and dynamic immunization schedules.
The database maintains structured document collections for users, doctors, appointments, slots, maternal records, and child immunizations.

The machine learning pipeline uses clinical features including Age, Gender, Blood Type, Medical Condition, Medication, and Test Results. Categorical variables are transformed using LabelEncoder. The dataset is split into 80% training and 20% testing subsets. Gradient Boosting Classifier models are trained for appointment type prediction (Emergency, Consultation, Follow-up, Vaccination, General Checkup) and clinical risk level scoring (Low, Moderate, High, Critical), achieving high classification accuracy.

The system implementation follows a 3-Tier Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture connecting React.js single-page applications, Express.js RESTful API services, Python Flask machine learning microservices, and MongoDB document databases.

4.3 MACHINE LEARNING TRIAGE & WORKLOAD RISK MICROSERVICE
Preprocesses raw patient clinical parameters (Age, Gender, Blood Type, Medical Condition, Medication, Test Results) for machine learning classification models.
Categorical string variables are cleaned and encoded using scikit-learn LabelEncoders. Features are formatted into numerical matrices before model fitting.
Uses Python pandas and scikit-learn preprocessing utilities. Encoded dictionary artifacts (encoders.pkl, label_encoder.pkl) are serialized for real-time Flask API execution.
Feature selection is performed to identify clinical variables relevant to appointment type prediction. The resulting feature matrix is supplied to the classification algorithms during model training.
Figure 4.7: Clinical Data Preprocessing & Feature Encoding Pipeline.
Predicts appointment urgency categories (Emergency, Consultation, Follow-up, Vaccination, General Checkup) using patient clinical parameters.
The prediction capability allows patient clinical parameters to be transformed into an estimated appointment urgency type and doctor workload risk score.
When an appointment is requested, input parameters are sent to Flask /predict-type. The Gradient Boosting Classifier predicts the urgency type and confidence score.
The prediction process begins with the required input variables. These inputs are prepared using the same feature-processing approach used during model development.
The processed values are passed to the selected classification model. The model generates a triage prediction, which is then returned to the React frontend interface and displayed to the user.
Models evaluated include Gradient Boosting Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, and Decision Trees. Gradient Boosting achieved top performance.

The models are trained using the training portion of the dataset and evaluated using the testing portion. Based on the implemented model comparison, Gradient Boosting Regressor is selected for the final prediction workflow.The prediction result can subsequently be used by other planning modules and visualized through the application.
Figure 4.8: Gradient Boosting Appointment Urgency Triage Prediction View.
Evaluates machine learning model classification metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score) to ensure accurate clinical triage.
Dataset is split 80:20 for training and testing. Models generate predictions on test samples, evaluated against ground truth labels.

After training, the models generate predictions for the testing dataset. Their performance is evaluated using the implemented regression metrics, such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and R² Score, where applicable.
The evaluation results are presented to the user through the clinical dashboard interface.
Gradient Boosting Classifier demonstrated superior performance across Emergency and Consultation classes compared to baseline models.

4.3.3 Doctor Workload Risk Scoring & Schedule Balancing
Calculates a cumulative workload risk score (0-100) for each doctor based on the clinical severity of their active appointments, assisting in schedule balancing.
Flask /doctor-risk-score receives patient profiles for a doctor's schedule. Gradient Boosting model evaluates risk scores (Low, Moderate, High, Critical) and computes average workload burden.
Workload risk score prevents doctor burnout and identifies overwhelmed departments, allowing admins to reassign slots.

Testing was conducted to verify that the Unified Healthcare Appointment and Immunization Tracking System operates reliably across all modules. Test cases cover user authentication, ABHA ID verification, multi-language UI switching, doctor slot management, appointment booking, unified medical history retrieval, emergency referral data transfer, maternal RCH ID tracking, child immunization status updates, node-cron background reminder triggers, ML appointment triage, and doctor workload risk scoring.
All test cases were executed against the MERN stack application and Python Flask ML microservice, verifying expected functional outputs and HTTP response statuses.
Individual API routes, Mongoose models, and Flask ML functions were tested independently with valid and edge-case inputs.

Different components are tested together. Example: Streamlit → FastAPI → Pydantic → SQLite, or Streamlit → ML prediction workflow → optimization workflow.Inter-module communication between React components, Express REST APIs, MongoDB database, and Flask ML microservice was verified.
End-to-end workflows from patient registration and appointment booking to clinical consultation and immunization status updating were tested.
Each feature was checked against defined functional requirements (FR1 to FR15).
Express and Flask REST endpoints were tested using Postman and client Axios calls for payload structure and HTTP status codes.
Machine learning models were evaluated on test datasets to verify classification accuracy, precision, and recall.

The Unified Healthcare Appointment and Immunization Tracking System successfully addresses the challenges of fragmented medical records, inefficient appointment scheduling, untracked maternal and child immunizations, language barriers, and unbalanced doctor consultation workloads. By integrating a MERN stack web platform with national ABHA digital health identities, node-cron automated background reminders, six-language localization, and a Python Flask machine learning microservice, the system provides a comprehensive technological solution for modern healthcare management.

The application features digital ABHA ID authentication, multi-language accessibility (English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam), unified medical history tracking across healthcare providers, emergency referral data sharing, maternal record linking via government RCH / PICME registration IDs, automated child vaccination schedules, background cron reminder dispatching, and machine learning triage using Gradient Boosting Classifiers. The ML service predicts appointment urgency types and computes doctor workload risk scores to optimize schedule distribution.

Built with React.js, TailwindCSS, Express.js, Node.js, MongoDB, node-cron, Flask, and scikit-learn, the platform demonstrates a modular, scalable architecture. Role-based access control and JWT authentication ensure data privacy and security. The system bridges the gap between patient access, clinical workflow, and administrative oversight.

By combining electronic health record continuity, predictive clinical machine learning, maternal-child health tracking, and robust RESTful API services, the system establishes a strong foundation for digital healthcare transformation.
The implemented system has been fully tested across unit, integration, functional, API, and machine learning evaluation criteria.
